newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open firmer amid shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open firmer amid shortcovering.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened firmer on Monday with many traders buying to cover short positions taken in the midst of the sharp market sell-off on Friday, analysts said.

"The way the market traded last week told me that there were a lot of traders just taking outright naked short positions so there's probably a bit of shortcovering this morning," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.39 to C$118.87 to yield 6.551 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 8/32 to yield 6.62 percent. The negative spread between the bonds was seven basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.
Canadian bonds plunged in price with U.S. Treasuries on Friday as the market there turned lower on new supply, a battered dollar, hedge fund selling and technically driven trades.

Dong said the Canadian market remains in a technically weak position and the risk remains to the downside following last week's sharp selloff. Bargain hunting by longer-term investors is helping boost prices this morning, he said.

Analysts said Canadian fixed-income markets are looking ahead to key U.S. economic data out later this week to provide direction. Key reports out this week include the U.S. retail sales report for July out Wednesday and the consumer price index for July out Thursday.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.02 to C$108.74 to yield 6.053 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.36 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 31 basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.
